create.name: Ajahn Achalo
create.bio:
Ajahn Achalo is a Theravada Buddhist monk in the Thai forest tradition of Ajahn Chah. He took full ordination at Wat Nong Pah Pong under Ajahn Liem, and over the years trained with Ajahn Sumedho, Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Jayasaro, in Thailand and in branch monasteries abroad, while looking to Ajahn Anan of Wat Marp Jan as his main mentor. In 2010 he founded Anandagiri Forest Monastery in the hills of Phetchabun province in northern Thailand, where he serves as abbot, and he became a Thai citizen in 2022.

His teaching centres on calm and insight meditation, loving-kindness and compassion practice, faith and devotion, and pilgrimage to the Buddhist holy places of India and China. Because the monastery is remote and the monks do not answer email, most people meet him through regular online gatherings on Zoom, recorded talks and guided meditations, and the occasional retreat in Malaysia or visit to the Buddhist Society of Victoria in Australia. In keeping with monastic custom everything is offered freely, including his autobiography, 10,000 Joys, 10,000 Sorrows, and a journal of three thousand hours of meditation at Bodh Gaya, which can be downloaded from his website.

free_resources.title: Ajahn Achalo on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: His talks and guided meditations on the Insight Timer app, free to play.

free_resources.title: Collection #1: Introductory Teachings and Guided Meditations
free_resources.description: Audio recordings of his early introductory talks with step-by-step guided meditations, free to stream or download from his website.

free_resources.title: 10,000 Joys, 10,000 Sorrows (Autobiography, Part One)
free_resources.description: The first part of his life story, from childhood to ordination and his years training with senior forest monks, offered as a free PDF.

free_resources.title: 3000 Hours of Meditation
free_resources.description: Journal entries from a long period of practice beside the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and a pilgrimage to the four holy sites, ending with advice on treating life itself as a pilgrimage. A free download.

free_resources.title: The Process of Realisation
free_resources.description: Twelve talks drawn from retreats, centre visits and pilgrimage, on refuge, generosity and ethics, the foundations of mindfulness and the qualities of the heart. A free ePub.

The email is Sister Joyce Lim's (a lay coordinator in Malaysia who handles online-meeting lists and in-person teaching enquiries), published as a mailto link (Cloudflare-obfuscated, decoded) on the enquiry page; the site says the monks themselves don't answer email. The enquiry form goes to the webmaster.

Base: the site says he founded and leads Anandagiri Forest Monastery in Petchabun province, Thailand, but names no town; city left null, country Thailand. The queue said Chiang Mai, which the site doesn't support. Regional: northern Thailand.
Honorific kept: 'Ajahn' is how he is known.
No paid offerings: as a monk he teaches free (online gatherings, talks, eBooks), so items are videos and free resources.
